q: 501. Septic tanks are best suited for ............
explain: Septic tanks are an on-site sanitation solution. They are ideal for isolated or scattered houses where a centralized underground sewerage system is not economically feasible.

q: 502. Septic tank effluent is ............
options: having fine organic solids with high B.O.D.
black tarry liquor with earthen odour
explain: The effluent from a septic tank still contains significant organic matter and pathogens. It usually has a high Biological Oxygen Demand (BOD) and requires further treatment in a soak pit or leach field.

q: 503. Media used in trickling filter is ............
explain: The filter media must be 'inert' (non-reactive) and tough to support the weight of the biofilm and the flow of sewage without breaking down.

q: 504. Usual size of media in standard rate trickling filter is ............
explain: Standard rate filters use larger media (25-100mm) to ensure large enough voids to prevent clogging from the growth of biological slime (zoogleal film).

q: 505. Depth of standard rate trickling filter is ............
explain: Trickling filters are generally deep enough to allow for sufficient contact time between the sewage and the biofilm; 1.5 to 4.8m is the common design range.

q: 506. Biological layer stickling to the trickling filter media consists of ............
explain: The 'zoogleal film' is a complex ecosystem containing various microorganisms like bacteria, fungi, and protozoa that feed on the organic matter in sewage.

q: 507. An extension of trickling filter is ............
explain: A Bio-tower is essentially a very tall trickling filter (up to 12m or more) using lightweight plastic media instead of stone.

q: 508. The primary operations in a trickling filter are ............
explain: Organic matter is first adsorbed/absorbed by the biological film and then broken down (oxidized) by the aerobic bacteria within that film.

q: 509. A very important character is media of a trickling filter is ............
explain: The more surface area available per unit volume, the more bacteria can grow, leading to higher treatment efficiency.

q: 510. Recirculation ratio for a standard rate trickling filter is ............
explain: Standard rate filters typically do not use recirculation; the sewage passes through the filter only once.

q: 511. A high rate biological treatment unit has a F/M ratio of ............
explain: The Food-to-Microorganism (F/M) ratio for conventional high-rate systems generally falls between 0.2 and 0.5 for stable operation.

q: 512. Effluent from a high rate trickling filter is ............
options: well nitrified and free from odours
explain: High-rate filters process sewage faster, which means the effluent is often less nitrified and slightly more turbid/brown compared to standard rate filters.

q: 513. Psychoda alternata is found in ............
explain: Psychoda alternata (the Filter Fly) is a common nuisance pest that breeds in the moist, organic environment of trickling filters.

q: 514. Filter unloading is ............
explain: Also known as 'sloughing', this is the process where the biological film becomes too heavy and detaches from the media, washing out with the effluent.

q: 515. To improve efficiency recirculation of the following is done in H.R. trickling filters ............
explain: In High-Rate filters, a portion of the treated effluent is pumped back to the inlet to dilute high-strength waste and keep the filter wet.

q: 516. The immediate layer sticking to the media of a trickling filter is of ............
explain: While the outer surface of the slime is aerobic, the layer directly touching the media is starved of oxygen and becomes anaerobic.

q: 517. An equivalent term of 'Mean cell residence time' is ............
explain: Mean Cell Residence Time (MCRT) is essentially the same as Solids Retention Time (SRT), representing the average time the bacteria stay in the system.

q: 518. Approximate percentage of the R.B.C. disc submerged under sewage is ............
explain: In a Rotating Biological Contactor (RBC), the discs are typically 40% submerged to allow the bacteria to alternate between feeding in the sewage and breathing in the air.

q: 519. In operation a R.B.C. is nearer to ............
explain: Like a trickling filter, RBC is an 'attached growth' system where the microbes stay fixed to a surface rather than floating in the water.

q: 520. Organic loading of RBC is expressed as ............
explain: Because it is a surface-based process, loading is measured by the amount of organic matter applied per unit area of the discs per day.

q: 521. Activated sludge process is a biological process involving ............
explain: ASP is a 'suspended growth' process that uses a diverse community of aerobic organisms to break down waste in an oxygen-rich environment.

q: 522. Media provided in A.S.P. is ............
explain: ASP does not use fixed media. The bacteria are kept in suspension through mechanical agitation or air bubbling.

q: 523. Efficiency of activated sludge process is ............
explain: When properly operated, ASP is highly efficient, typically removing 90-95% of the BOD from the influent sewage.

q: 524. Conventional ASP is not suited to ............
options: strong loading and varying quality of influent
shock loading and varying quality of influent
explain: Conventional ASP is sensitive; a 'shock' of toxic chemicals or a sudden surge in volume can kill the bacteria or wash them out of the system.

q: 525. Sludge from a Biological treatment unit is ............
options: rich in organic matter and bacteria
rich in inorganic matter and micro organisms
explain: This sludge (secondary sludge) is primarily composed of the excess microorganisms that have grown by eating the organic waste.

q: 526. A treatment unit development on algal-bacteria mutual symbiosis is ............
explain: In oxidation ponds (WSP), algae produce oxygen through photosynthesis which is used by bacteria, while bacteria produce CO2 used by algae.

q: 527. Sludge digestion is ............
options: removal of waste products from sludge
explain: Digestion is the process of 'stabilizing' the sludge—making it non-putrescible and reducing its volume and pathogen content.

q: 528. Anaerobic sludge digestion mainly yields ............
explain: The most significant byproduct is Methane (approx 65%), which is a useful fuel gas (biogas).

q: 529. Usually the digesters have a dia of ............
explain: Standard circular sludge digesters are typically built within the diameter range of 6 to 35 meters.

q: 530. Supernatant from a digester will be having a B.O.D. of ............
explain: The liquor (supernatant) that settles on top of the digesting sludge is extremely polluted, often exceeding 5000 mg/l BOD.

q: 531. Dried sludge is a good ............
options: filler of a low lying area
explain: Digested and dried sludge contains organic matter that improves soil structure and moisture retention, acting as a 'soil builder' or conditioner.

q: 532. Pedestal type commode is ............
options: partly above and partly below floor level
explain: The pedestal (Western-style) toilet sits entirely on top of the finished floor level.

q: 533. Any trap is intended to trap ............
explain: The sole purpose of a plumbing trap is to prevent foul-smelling and toxic sewer gases from entering the building.

q: 534. Any trap should necessarily have ............
explain: A water seal (the standing water in the 'U' bend) is what physically blocks the passage of gases.

q: 535. The last trap provided in a house drainage system is ............
explain: The intercepting trap is located at the point where the house drain connects to the public sewer to keep public sewer gases out of the house pipes.

q: 536. Stall type urinals are best suited to ............
explain: Stall urinals extend to the floor, making them robust and suitable for high-traffic public areas.

q: 537. Bowl type urinals are ideal for ............
explain: Bowl urinals can be mounted at varying heights to accommodate both adults and children.

q: 538. Soil stack collects waste waters from ............
explain: A 'soil pipe' is specifically designed to carry 'night soil' or waste containing human excreta from toilets.

q: 539. Waste pipe collects liquid waste from ............
explain: Waste pipes carry 'sullage'—wastewater that does not contain human excreta, such as from sinks, basins, and showers.

q: 540. The pipe having min. dia. in plumbing system is ............
explain: Anti-syphonage pipes are smaller air vents (usually 32-50mm) that preserve the water seal in traps by preventing vacuum formation.

q: 541. Anti-syphonage pipe need not be provided in ............
explain: In single-story houses with a simple drain layout, the risk of 'siphoning' a trap dry is much lower, so air vents are sometimes omitted.

q: 542. The object of cowl is to ............
options: prevent entry of rainfall into the waste pipe
explain: A cowl or wire balloon is placed on top of vent pipes to prevent birds from building nests and clogging the airway.

q: 543. The solid waste resulting from growing, handling, preparation, cooking and consumption of putrescible organic matter is called ............
explain: Garbage is the technical term for biodegradable organic waste that can rot and cause odors.

q: 544. Pieces of papers, crockery, scrap metals etc., are classified as ............
explain: Rubbish refers to non-putrescible (non-rotting) solid waste, which can be either combustible (paper) or non-combustible (metal/glass).

q: 545. Salvaging is ............
options: sanitary land filling of solid waste
explain: Salvaging (or recycling) is the recovery of valuable materials from the waste stream for reuse.

q: 546. Agent responsible for ecological imbalance is ............
explain: Human activities like industrialization, deforestation, and pollution are the primary drivers of modern ecological instability.

q: 547. The activity that may not affect ecological balance is ............
explain: Small-scale gardening and landscaping are generally considered positive or neutral activities that do not disrupt large-scale ecosystems.

q: 548. Eco system is ............
explain: An ecosystem is defined by the interaction of a biological community (species) with their physical environment (habitat).

q: 549. The relationship between 'Biotic' and 'Abiotic' substances of an ecosystem is ............
explain: Reciprocity refers to the mutual exchange between living things (biotic) and the non-living environment (abiotic), such as nutrient cycling.

q: 550. 'Ecological niche' is ............
options: community and environment of an organism
confinement of a species to a specific region
explain: While often used for the 'job' a species does, in this context, it refers to the specific physical space and role an organism occupies.

options: is transfer of energy from one organism to another
is relationship between producers, herbivores and carnivores
is comprising of any three or more organisms
is combination of organisms at different trophic levels
explain: A food chain represents the sequence of who eats whom, tracking the one-way flow of energy from the sun through various living things.

q: 552. 'A nectar sipping butterfly -> Dragon fly -> Frog -> Snake -> Hawk' is ............
explain: This is a grazing or predator food chain because it starts with a producer and moves up through successive levels of predators.

q: 553. 'Biological magnification' is ............
options: decrease in concentration with trophic level
increase in concentration with trophic level
explain: Biomagnification is the process where certain toxins (like mercury or DDT) become more concentrated as they move up the food chain.

q: 554. An effective method of controlling eutrophication of lake water ............
options: diluting with nutrient free water very often
explain: Eutrophication is caused by excess nutrients (Nitrogen/Phosphorus). Diluting the lake with fresh, nutrient-poor water helps reduce the algal blooms.
